name: MD-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Olszewski has a roughly 50-to-1 fundraising advantage, with over $1 million raised and $614,000 on hand versus about $20,000 for Wallace
The district leans Democratic by about ten points and the incumbent is running for re-election
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 95%, with no outside spending to change the picture
No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, leaving the outlook resting on fundamentals
model.rationale: Olszewski combines a D+10 district, incumbency, and an overwhelming money advantage over a barely funded challenger, and markets price his re-election around 95% or better. With no polling suggesting competition and no outside spending on either side, the structural evidence points to a comfortable double-digit win.
model.watch: A wave of late outside spending against Olszewski or a sharply Republican-favorable national environment could narrow what is currently a lopsided race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Johnny Olszewski, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a Maryland district that leans Democratic by about ten points. He has raised more than $1 million and enters the fall with over $600,000 on hand, while Republican Dave Wallace has raised about $20,000 and reports roughly $3,000 in the bank. No outside groups are spending meaningfully in the race, and prediction markets give Olszewski about a 95% chance of winning.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the district, so the outlook rests on district lean, incumbency, and the money gap, all of which favor the Democrat. The expected margin is roughly twenty points, in line with recent Democratic performance in Baltimore-area districts. A Republican upset would require a dramatic shift in the national environment or unexpected spending that neither side currently shows signs of making.
